title: Wire fetchers to Store; log queries including empty results
description:
Today every fetcher returns list[Record] and drops it: grep shows zero importers of einstein.store outside tests/. Each sandbox worker is a fresh container, so every run re-fetches from zero and burns the USPTO/GitHub key quota on data already seen. einstein-2 already built the cache (records keyed by (type,id), full response in Record.raw, first_seen/last_seen); nothing calls it. Do not build a second cache -- wire this one.

The part the current schema does NOT cover, and the reason this is P1 rather than an optimization:

A SEARCH THAT RETURNS NOTHING LEAVES NO TRACE. Zero results produce zero Records, so nothing is written. But an empty search IS the novelty claim -- 'no patent connects method M to domain B' is precisely a query that came back empty. Under today's schema that claim is unreproducible: nothing distinguishes 'never queried' from 'queried, found nothing' from 'queried, got a 429 and swallowed it'. The auditor in einstein-16 will assert absence from a record that does not exist.

So add a queries table: query string, source, params (max_results etc.), fetched_at, status (ok | rate_limited | error), and the ids returned -- possibly none. An empty ok row is the evidence for a negative finding; a rate_limited row is NOT evidence of anything and must never be read as one.

CACHED NEGATIVES DECAY AND POSITIVES DO NOT. A patent found last month is still a patent. An empty result from last month is not still empty -- patents publish continuously, so a stale empty row silently becomes a false novelty claim. Negative rows need a TTL (start at 30 days, make it a parameter, document the unit); positive rows do not. Every consumer of an absence gets fetched_at alongside it and treats the claim as valid-as-of that date, not as timeless.

ACCEPTANCE:
- fetch_patents / fetch_repos / arXiv+OpenAlex fetchers persist Records through Store on the fetch path, and a second identical fetch reads from the store rather than the network (assert the fake HTTP client is called once across two calls).
- A zero-result search writes a queries row with status=ok and no ids; a 429 writes status=rate_limited and is not readable as a negative finding. Both asserted.
- Reading a negative older than the TTL reports it as expired, not as absent. Asserted with an injected clock, not a sleep.
- No network in the suite; the recorded responses land in tests/fixtures/ (currently empty).

Same captures feed the positive arm of einstein-0.1 -- one capture, three uses (cache, fixtures, benchmark). No hard dependency edge on 0.1 because it is already in flight.
close_reason: Fetchers wired to Store; queries table logs zero-result/rate_limited outcomes; TTL-expiry verified with injected clock; fixtures added; 220 tests pass (2 pre-existing unrelated test_cli.py failures filed as einstein-21.1)

title: Gap-detection evaluation harness with a genuine negative arm
description:
einstein-11 only proves the classifier runs (fixture data yields 3 classes). It says nothing about whether a detected gap is real. The system's output is a claim about ABSENCE -- 'no repo/patent connects method M to domain B' -- made from a partial index over throttled APIs. That is a miss-rate claim, and a miss-rate claim with no labeled negatives is unfalsifiable.

Build the benchmark BEFORE any agent node consumes Gap records, otherwise the ideator/auditor loop launders an unmeasured signal into confident prose.

Two arms, both required:

POSITIVE ARM -- known connections the detector must NOT flag as a gap. Harvest pairs where a paper and a repo (or a patent) are known-linked: arXiv entries with a Papers-with-Code / linked GitHub repo, or patents citing a specific arXiv ID. These are ground-truth NON-gaps. Every one the detector calls a gap is a false discovery.

NEGATIVE ARM -- the hard part, and the reason mathgraph's benchmark was worth building. Sample paper x repo pairs at random from unrelated domains: genuinely unconnected, and the detector should flag them. If it flags random pairs at the same rate it flags the curated cross-pollination candidates, the score is measuring topic distance, not opportunity, and the whole gap thesis is dead.

REPORT, per threshold: false-discovery rate on the positive arm, flag rate on the negative arm, and the abstention rate (pairs where the score falls in the ambiguous band and no claim is made). Sweep the threshold and publish the curve, not one operating point.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Both arms are checked-in fixtures with recorded API responses. No network in the test suite.
- One command regenerates every number, and that command is named in the README next to each figure.
- The README states the measured false-discovery rate and whether an operating point exists where the detector is trustworthy. If none exists, that is the finding and it gets published as the finding -- do not tune until a demo looks good.
- An 'abstain' outcome is a first-class Gap classification, not an error case.

Prior art in your own repos: mathgraph/evaluate.py + bench_pfr.py are exactly this shape (negative arm, three-valued matched/ambiguous/unmatched scorer), and its result was negative -- ~15%% max precision, no trustworthy operating point. Expect the same until measured otherwise. certabstain/conformal.py is how the threshold gets a guarantee instead of a guess.
notes:
Verified prior in-progress work (found already in tree, untracked, no bd notes from previous session): einstein/gap_benchmark.py, tests/test_gap_benchmark.py, scripts/harvest_gap_benchmark.py, tests/fixtures/gap_benchmark.json (19 positive + 19 negative real paper<->repo pairs harvested once from live arXiv/GitHub APIs), and a README benchmark section were all already implemented. Independently re-ran and confirmed every claim before closing:
- 'uv run python -m unittest discover tests' -> 220 tests, OK (includes 17 in test_gap_benchmark.py), no network calls.
- 'uv run python -m einstein.gap_benchmark' output matches README numbers exactly: FDR=0.37/flag_rate=1.00 at threshold=0.20; floor FDR=0.16 (3/19) at threshold=0.02; no (margin,threshold) in the swept grid clears the trustworthy bar (FDR<=0.10, flag_rate>=0.90).
- Spot-checked the '3 papers score exactly 0.0 similarity against their own repo' claim by direct script run: confirmed IDs are 2102.12092 (DALL-E), 2010.11929 (ViT), 1701.07875 (WGAN) -- matches README exactly.
- Confirmed fixture is real fetched data (not fabricated): BERT abstract text matches known paper, arxiv 'raw' field has authors/categories/entry_id from live API.
- All 4 acceptance bullets met: checked-in fixtures with no test-suite network; single regenerating command named next to every README figure; README states the negative finding explicitly (no trustworthy operating point) rather than tuning to a demo; gap_benchmark.classify() treats 'abstain' as a first-class three-valued outcome, not an exception path.
- mathgraph/ and certabstain/ referenced in the bead body are not present in this checkout; README already states this rather than fabricating a conformal-threshold guarantee. No action possible there.
Did not modify any code -- only verified. Handoff written to sandbox-handoffs/einstein-0.1.md.

title: Sandboxed execution + self-heal loop
description: Run generated code in an isolated subprocess/container against qiskit-aer. Feed stderr back to the codegen agent, retry up to N times. Without this the pipeline ships non-functional code and calls it a win. Acceptance: deliberately broken snippet is repaired or fails after N with the traceback recorded.

title: LangGraph state machine skeleton
description: AgentState TypedDict + StateGraph wiring ingest -> analyze -> conditional route -> agents -> END. Conditional edge short-circuits to END when zero gaps so no LLM tokens burn. Acceptance: graph compiles and runs end-to-end on fixture data with zero gaps.
close_reason: LangGraph state machine skeleton implemented: einstein/graph.py wires ingest -> analyze -> conditional route -> agents -> END. Conditional edge short-circuits to END on zero gaps (agents node never called, verified by test). Full suite: 132 tests pass.

title: Pluggable embedding backend (TF-IDF default, dense swappable)
description: embed(texts) -> matrix behind one interface. Start TF-IDF; sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM as a drop-in. Single shared vector space fitted over all sources. Acceptance: swapping backend changes no caller code.
close_reason: einstein/embedding.py implements the Embedder protocol (fit/transform/fit_transform), TfidfEmbedder default backend, SentenceTransformerEmbedder drop-in dense backend behind a guarded optional import, and embed_groups() fitting one shared vector space over all source groups. Acceptance criterion (swapping backend changes no caller code) directly tested in tests/test_embedding.py::test_backend_swap_changes_no_caller_code using a third non-sklearn FakeWordCountEmbedder against the same embed_groups() call. Full suite: 12/12 embedding tests pass, 44/44 overall.

title: Three-way gap detection matrix
description: paper x repo and paper x patent cosine matrices. Classify: (low repo, low patent) = true invention gap; (low repo, high patent) = open-source disruption target; plus unformalized-code per repo. Emit structured Gap records, not print statements. Acceptance: fixture data yields the expected 3 classes.
notes: Implemented einstein/gaps.py: detect_gaps(papers, repos, patents, repo_threshold, patent_threshold, embedder=None) builds paper x repo and paper x patent cosine matrices via embed_groups (shared TF-IDF space by default) and emits Gap dataclass records (kind, subject_type/id/title, tuple of Match evidence with against_type/best_id/best_similarity/threshold). Three GAP_KINDS: true_invention_gap (low repo, low patent), open_source_disruption_target (low repo, high patent), unformalized_code (repo with no close paper, read from the same matrix by column). Gap.gap_key/to_payload feed Store.upsert_gap unchanged. tests/test_gaps.py: 24 tests incl. fixture data hitting all 3 classes, Store round-trip/idempotency, empty-corpus edge cases, bad-type assertions. Full suite: 108 tests, OK. No new deps (sklearn/numpy already pinned).

title: GitHub fetcher
description: GitHub search API (repositories) -> Record; text = name + description + topics. Read GITHUB_TOKEN from env, handle non-200 and rate-limit headers instead of silently returning empty. Acceptance: non-200 raises/logs distinctly from zero-results.
close_reason: GitHub repo search fetcher implemented in einstein/github_fetcher.py: fetch_repos(query) hits GET /search/repositories, maps items to Record(type=repo, id=full_name, title=full_name, summary=description+topics, url=html_url, ts=pushed_at, raw=item). Reads GITHUB_TOKEN from env for Bearer auth (optional). Non-200 raises GitHubFetchError(status_code, rate_limited=...) distinct from a genuine zero-results 200 (which returns []); 429 and 403-with-X-RateLimit-Remaining:0 are flagged rate_limited=True and logged at warning, other non-200s logged at error. 24 new unit tests in tests/test_github_fetcher.py using a fake HTTP client (no network in the suite) cover success mapping, auth header presence/absence, zero-results, and every non-200/rate-limit path. Full suite: 36 passed. Verified against the live API by hand (not part of the test suite): search for 'quantum error correction' returned 3 real repos with valid ISO ts; a malformed query ('repo:') returned a real 422 -> GitHubFetchError, proving the non-200-vs-zero-results distinction holds against the real API, not just fakes.

title: USPTO patents fetcher
description: USPTO Open Data Portal search -> Record. Real API key handling; REMOVE the mock-patent fallback from the convo draft - silent fake data poisons the gap matrix. Fail loud instead. Acceptance: missing key raises a clear error.
close_reason: USPTO fetcher implemented in einstein/uspto_fetcher.py: fetch_patents() raises USPTOFetchError(missing_key=True) before any HTTP call if no USPTO_API_KEY env var / api_key arg is set. No mock-patent fallback exists anywhere in the codebase (grep confirms only mentions are in gemini_convo.md draft and test/docstring references to what was removed). 84/84 tests pass.

title: arXiv fetcher
description: arxiv.Client search by query, sort SubmittedDate, map to Record. Handle empty results and API throttling. Acceptance: returns >=1 Record for 'quantum error correction'.
close_reason: arXiv fetcher implemented: einstein/arxiv_fetcher.py fetch_papers() using arxiv.Client, sorted by SubmittedDate, mapped to Record. Tests in tests/test_arxiv_fetcher.py (16 tests, no network). Acceptance criterion verified live: fetch_papers('quantum error correction') returned 3 Records.

title: Define normalized Record schema + repo skeleton
description: One dataclass/TypedDict shared by every source: {type: paper|repo|patent, id, title, summary, url, ts, raw}. Every fetcher returns list[Record]. Pin deps (requests, arxiv, scikit-learn, numpy, pandas). Acceptance: schema module imports clean, one assert-based self-check.
close_reason: Record schema (einstein/schema.py) implemented: frozen dataclass with type/id/title/summary/url/ts/raw fields, assert-based validation in __post_init__, assert-based self-check under __main__, plus a unittest suite. Deps pinned in pyproject.toml (requests, arxiv, scikit-learn, numpy, pandas). Full suite green: 10 passed.

title: EPIC: Invention gap-detection pipeline (arXiv x GitHub x Patents -> agentic ideation)
description: End-to-end system from gemini_convo.md: ingest arXiv/GitHub/USPTO/OpenAlex, normalize, embed, detect structural gaps, then run a multi-agent ideation loop (ideator -> novelty auditor -> feasibility -> codegen -> sandboxed validation). Parent epic for all pipeline stages.

title: test_cli.py: ArxivFetchError construction missing required query/cause kwargs
description: tests/test_cli.py:108 and :193 construct ArxivFetchError("boom") with only a message, but einstein/arxiv_fetcher.py's ArxivFetchError requires keyword-only query= and cause=. uv run python -m unittest discover tests currently fails these 2 with TypeError. Found incidentally while working einstein-0.2 (store/fetcher wiring); not touched since cli.py/test_cli.py belong to einstein-21's in-flight scope.
notes: Fixed both ArxivFetchError('boom') call sites in tests/test_cli.py (lines 108, 193) to pass required kwargs query='optimization' and cause=Exception('boom'). Full suite: uv run python -m unittest discover tests -> Ran 220 tests in 0.326s, OK.

title: Port mathgraph sandbox harness (sandbox.sh, prompt, uv lock) to einstein
description: einstein already has beads/uv/.claude/.codex parity with mathgraph. Missing: sandbox.sh worker loop, sandbox-prompt.md standing context, uv.lock/.venv, gitignore entries for sandbox output. App Dockerfile deliberately deferred until there is a CLI to containerize.

title: Proposal report output
description: Emit validated proposals as structured JSON + markdown: gap classification, novelty verdict, feasibility, working code, run evidence.

title: Code generation agent node (Python/Qiskit)
description: Synthesize a reference implementation from the surviving proposal. Prompt carries extracted math; target library version pinned explicitly - deprecated-API drift is the top failure mode.

title: Novelty auditor agent node
description: Adversarial reviewer: re-queries Semantic Scholar + patent claims to DISPROVE novelty. Reject or force-pivot above similarity threshold theta. Uses independent claims for infringement reasoning.

title: Feasibility evaluator agent node
description: Assess compute requirements, dataset availability, practical constraints. Outputs go/no-go plus an execution blueprint.

title: Ideator agent node
description: Turn a Gap record into a structured problem-solution pair (Method M + Problem P). Context includes extracted equations, not just the abstract.

title: Method-domain cross-pollination detection
description: Rule A: method M embedding close to domain B space but zero citation/graph edge between them. Needs citation edges + embeddings. This is where non-obvious inventions come from, not same-keyword matching.

title: Gap dedup + temporal velocity scoring
description: Diff new gaps against the seen-gaps table. Score by dormancy (0 repos for 2y = dormant target) vs activity (commits rising = someone is already building it). Prevents regenerating last week's ideas.

title: Patent independent-claims extraction
description: Parse claims section, isolate independent claims. Abstract-level TF-IDF is useless for patent law; claim text is what the novelty auditor needs.
close_reason: Implemented einstein/patent_claims.py: parse_claims()/independent_claims() split claims-section text into numbered Claims and classify independent vs dependent by claim-number back-reference (single ref, and-lists, hyphen/to ranges, 'any of the preceding claims', canceled-claim handling); independent_claims_for_record() reads claim text from Record.raw without ever falling back to the abstract. 23 new tests, 170/170 total pass (uv run python -m unittest discover tests).

title: OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar fetcher + citation edges
description: Pull works + referenced_works to build a citation adjacency table. Feeds cross-pollination detection. Acceptance: one seed DOI returns >0 outbound citation edges.
notes: Implemented einstein/openalex_fetcher.py: fetch_work_by_doi (DOI -> Record via OpenAlex works API, abstract reconstructed from abstract_inverted_index) and fetch_citation_edges (seed DOI -> list[Edge] from referenced_works). 16 new tests in tests/test_openalex_fetcher.py, all against a fixture mirroring the real API shape -- no network in the suite. Verified live by hand against https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.7717/peerj.4375: 54 outbound edges, matching fixture assumptions exactly. Full suite: 57 tests OK.
close_reason: OpenAlex fetcher + citation edges implemented and verified against the live API; acceptance criterion (seed DOI -> >0 outbound edges) confirmed both in tests (fixture) and live (54 edges for 10.7717/peerj.4375).

title: arXiv full-text / LaTeX source extraction
description: Pull /e-print/ tarball, extract LaTeX, isolate math blocks (Hamiltonians, unitaries, cost functions) and Limitations/Future Work sections. Abstracts alone lose the actual mechanics. Acceptance: for one known paper, extracted equation count > 0.
close_reason: Acceptance met: tests/test_arxiv_source.py::EquationExtractionTest::test_known_paper_yields_equations builds a fixture tarball from a real published equation (arXiv:1706.03762 scaled dot-product attention) and asserts extracted equation count > 0 via extract_source(), no network. 11 new tests total (equation extraction, tagging, limitations/future-work section isolation, multi-file concatenation, PDF-only NoTexSourceError, non-tarball fallback, non-200 ArxivSourceError). Full suite: 231 tests OK (uv run python -m unittest discover tests).

title: Local persistence layer (SQLite) for records + seen-gaps
description: Single SQLite file: records table keyed by (source,id), gaps table with first_seen/last_seen. Kills the statelessness gap from the convo. ponytail: SQLite not Neo4j until graph traversal actually needs it. Acceptance: upsert twice -> one row, timestamps updated.
notes: Added einstein/store.py (SQLite Store class, records+gaps tables, upsert with first_seen/last_seen) and tests/test_store.py (12 tests). Keyed records on (type,id) not (source,id) since Record has no source field -- documented rationale in handoff. Full suite: 68 tests, OK. See sandbox-handoffs/einstein-2.md.
close_reason: Acceptance criterion met: upsert twice yields one row with first_seen preserved and last_seen updated, verified in tests/test_store.py and python -m einstein.store self-check. Full suite green: 68 tests OK.

title: CLI entrypoint + scheduled run
description: One CLI: domain, thresholds, source toggles. Then cron/Actions for nightly runs. ponytail: cron before Airflow/Prefect - a DAG engine for a linear pipeline is 3am-page material.

title: Constraint & friction mining
description: Extract Limitations/Future Work/Open Problems from papers (needs einstein-7) plus GitHub issues labeled help-wanted/bug. Cluster pain points across repos/papers to find widespread bottlenecks.
